title: Article 19 — Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.

content.overview: Article 19 guarantees to citizens the freedoms of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession, subject to the reasonable restrictions authorised by clauses (2) to (6). Non-citizens do not hold Article 19 rights. Restrictions must be grounded in the specific grounds listed in the Constitution and must be reasonable.

sections.heading: Freedoms
sections.body: Article 19(1) lists the freedoms. Each freedom has corresponding restriction clauses. Verify the official text for the exact catalogue and grounds.

sections.heading: Reasonable restrictions
sections.body: Restrictions must fall within the enumerated grounds and must be reasonable. Reasonableness is examined in light of the purpose and the means. Verify current clause text in the official Constitution.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Identify which freedom is engaged, which restriction clause is invoked, and why the restriction is or is not reasonable. Citizens only. Pair with Articles 14 and 21 where the golden-triangle analysis applies.
